## `src/operations/activation.rs`

Activation and trigonometric graph operations used by model execution.

Direct operations map to declarations in `mlx-c/mlx/c/ops.h` and forwarding definitions in `mlx-c/mlx/c/ops.cpp`. Composite GELU functions intentionally stay expressed as MLX graph operations so MLX controls dtype promotion, kernel selection, and BF16 rounding; do not replace their internals with Rust scalar math over copied device values.

### `MlxBindingsContext::softplus`

```rust
pub fn softplus(&self, input: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies numerically stable softplus through MLX `logaddexp(input, 0)`.

This matches MLX's `nn.softplus`, which delegates to `logaddexp(x, 0)`. The naive `log1p(exp(x))` overflows to infinity for large positive inputs (x > ~88 in float32), which corrupts gated-delta decay values during long-context prefill.

### `MlxBindingsContext::silu`

```rust
pub fn silu(&self, input: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies the SiLU activation as `x * sigmoid(x)` on the MLX stream.

### `MlxBindingsContext::tanh`

```rust
pub fn tanh(&self, input: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies the elementwise tanh function on the MLX stream.

### `MlxBindingsContext::erf`

```rust
pub fn erf(&self, input: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies the elementwise error function through MLX-C `mlx_erf`.

### `MlxBindingsContext::cos`

```rust
pub fn cos(&self, input: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies the elementwise cosine through MLX-C `mlx_cos`.

### `MlxBindingsContext::sin`

```rust
pub fn sin(&self, input: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies the elementwise sine through MLX-C `mlx_sin`.

### `MlxBindingsContext::power`

```rust
pub fn power(&self, bases: &MlxArray, exponents: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Raises each broadcast-compatible base through MLX-C `mlx_power`.

Using `mlx_power(x, 3)` rather than spelling `x*x*x` is deliberate. MLX's power kernel follows a different BF16 rounding path, and the vision GELU parity reference was generated with that operation.

### `MlxBindingsContext::gelu`

```rust
pub fn gelu(&self, input: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies exact GELU while preserving the activation dtype.

Formula: `0.5*x*(1 + erf(x/sqrt(2)))`. MLX-C exposes `mlx_erf` but no single exact-GELU C entry point, so this composes `mlx_multiply`, `mlx_add`, and `mlx_erf`. The Qwen3.5 vision patch merger requires exact GELU.

### `MlxBindingsContext::gelu_tanh`

```rust
pub fn gelu_tanh(&self, input: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies the GELU activation using the PyTorch tanh approximation.

`GELU(x) = 0.5 * x * (1 + tanh(sqrt(2/pi) * (x + 0.044715 * x^3)))`

### `MlxBindingsContext::apply_softplus_attention_gate`

```rust
pub fn apply_softplus_attention_gate(&self, attention_output: &MlxArray, gate_logits: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies `attention_output * softplus(gate_logits)` without widening output storage.

### `MlxBindingsContext::unique`

```rust
pub fn unique(&self, a: &MlxArray, size: i32, return_index: bool, return_inverse: bool, return_counts: bool, fill_value: Option<&MlxArray>) -> Result<MlxArrayVector, MlxCError>
```

Applies MLX-C `mlx_unique`. `size` is the exact unique count the result carries: fewer actual uniques get padded (with `fill_value` when supplied), so callers either know the count a priori or pass the array size and trim. The returned vector carries the unique values first, then the `return_index`, `return_inverse`, and `return_counts` arrays in that order when requested.

## `src/operations/attention.rs`

Validated wrappers over MLX's fused scaled dot-product attention.

C ABI: `mlx-c/mlx/c/fast.h::mlx_fast_scaled_dot_product_attention`. C++ bridge: `mlx-c/mlx/c/fast.cpp`, forwarding to `mlx::core::fast::scaled_dot_product_attention`. MLX computes attention as `softmax(scale * Q @ K^T + mask) @ V` and performs softmax in Float32 even for BF16 inputs. Model code should shape/pad/segment tensors, not reproduce this math. Callers can select unmasked, causal, or explicit array-mask execution.

### `MlxBindingsContext::scaled_dot_product_attention`

```rust
pub fn scaled_dot_product_attention(&self, queries: &MlxArray, keys: &MlxArray, values: &MlxArray, scale: f32) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies MLX-C fused unmasked attention over `[batch, heads, length, width]`.

Q heads may be a multiple of K/V heads for grouped-query attention.

### `MlxBindingsContext::causal_scaled_dot_product_attention`

```rust
pub fn causal_scaled_dot_product_attention(&self, queries: &MlxArray, keys: &MlxArray, values: &MlxArray, scale: f32) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies causal scaled dot-product attention without an explicit mask array.

### `MlxBindingsContext::masked_scaled_dot_product_attention`

```rust
pub fn masked_scaled_dot_product_attention(&self, queries: &MlxArray, keys: &MlxArray, values: &MlxArray, scale: f32, mask: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies fused attention with a broadcast-compatible boolean or additive mask.

## `src/operations/convolution.rs`

Thin validated wrappers over MLX-C convolution operations.

C declarations: `mlx-c/mlx/c/ops.h::{mlx_conv1d, mlx_conv2d, mlx_conv3d}`. C++ forwarding definitions: `mlx-c/mlx/c/ops.cpp`. MLX uses channel-last inputs: Conv1d `[N,L,C]`, Conv2d `[N,H,W,C]`, and Conv3d `[N,D,H,W,C]`. Weights begin with output channels and end with input channels per group. These layouts differ from PyTorch.

### `MlxBindingsContext::conv1d`

```rust
pub fn conv1d(&self, input: &MlxArray, weight: &MlxArray, stride: i32, padding: i32, dilation: i32, groups: i32) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies MLX one-dimensional convolution over `[batch, length, channels]` inputs.

### `MlxBindingsContext::conv2d`

```rust
pub fn conv2d(&self, input: &MlxArray, weight: &MlxArray, strides: [i32; 2], paddings: [i32; 2], dilations: [i32; 2], groups: i32) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies MLX two-dimensional convolution over `[batch, height, width, channels]`.

### `MlxBindingsContext::conv3d`

```rust
pub fn conv3d(&self, input: &MlxArray, weight: &MlxArray, strides: [i32; 3], paddings: [i32; 3], dilations: [i32; 3], groups: i32) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies MLX-C `mlx_conv3d` over `[batch, depth, height, width, channels]`.

The Qwen3.5-MoE vision tower uses kernel=stride=`[temporal, patch, patch]`, so this operation projects disjoint patch volumes rather than sliding over neighboring pixels.

## `src/operations/fast_primitives.rs`

MLX's fast primitives without a family of their own: the gated-delta update and fused cross entropy.

### `MlxBindingsContext::gated_delta_update`

```rust
pub fn gated_delta_update(&self, queries: &MlxArray, keys: &MlxArray, values: &MlxArray, gates: &MlxArray, beta: &MlxArray, initial_state: Option<&MlxArray>, mask: Option<&MlxArray>) -> Result<MlxArrayVector, MlxCError>
```

Applies MLX-C `mlx_fast_gated_delta_update`, returning the outputs first and the final recurrent state second.

`queries` and `keys` are shaped `(batch, steps, key_heads, key_dims)`, `values` is `(batch, steps, value_heads, value_dims)`, `gates` and `beta` are `(batch, steps, value_heads)`, and `initial_state` is `(batch, value_heads, value_dims, key_dims)`, zero when absent. `mask` is a boolean `(batch, steps)` selecting the steps that update the state.

**Errors:** Returns the captured MLX-C description when the graph cannot be built.

### `MlxBindingsContext::fast_cross_entropy`

```rust
pub fn fast_cross_entropy(&self, logits: &MlxArray, targets: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies MLX-C `mlx_fast_cross_entropy` over `logits` and class `targets`.

**Errors:** Returns the captured MLX-C description when the graph cannot be built.

### `MlxBindingsContext::gather_dense_matmul`

```rust
pub fn gather_dense_matmul(&self, left: &MlxArray, right: &MlxArray, left_indices: Option<&MlxArray>, right_indices: Option<&MlxArray>, sorted_indices: bool) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Builds matrix multiplication while selecting matrix batches on-device.

This maps directly to MLX `gather_mm`; unlike `take` followed by `matmul`, it does not materialize one weight matrix per assignment.

### `MlxBindingsContext::addmm`

```rust
pub fn addmm(&self, bias: &MlxArray, left: &MlxArray, right: &MlxArray, alpha: f32, beta: f32) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies MLX-C `mlx_addmm`: `alpha * (left @ right) + beta * bias`.

See `mlx-c/mlx/c/ops.h::mlx_addmm` and its forwarding implementation in `ops.cpp`. Keep affine model layers on this fused operation: separate `mlx_matmul` then `mlx_add` changes BF16 accumulation/rounding and violates the Qwen3.5 vision numerical contract.

### `MlxBindingsContext::take_axis`

```rust
pub fn take_axis(&self, input: &MlxArray, indices: &MlxArray, axis: i32) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Selects indices along one array axis through MLX-C `mlx_take_axis`.

Qwen3.5-MoE uses this for learned positions, quantized text embeddings, and the dense global-expert-ID to compact-page-slot lookup used by paged expert execution. This call records a lazy MLX operation on this context's stream; it does not copy indices to Rust or synchronously evaluate the resulting array.


### `MlxBindingsContext::scatter_add`

```rust
pub fn scatter_add(&self, input: &MlxArray, indices: &MlxArray, updates: &MlxArray, axis: i32) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Adds `updates` into a copy of `input` at `indices` along one axis.

Compact mixture-of-experts split reduction lands several assignment rows on the same token. `put_along_axis` overwrites; this keeps every routed expert's contribution. MLX requires `updates.ndim() == input.ndim() + indices.ndim()`. For destination `[token_rows, hidden]`, pass indices `[assignment_count]` and updates `[assignment_count, 1, hidden]`.

## `src/operations/upstream_gap.rs`

Gap-shim wrappers: the Rust path to MLX functions the vendored MLX-C pin has not wrapped.

Each wrapper calls this repository's own `mlxrs_*` C ABI (the `native_gap_shim` component compiled by the native build engine) with the same owned-handle and captured-error semantics as every MLX-C family. The shim exists so an MLX capability is reachable the day the pin moves; when an MLX-C release wraps a function, the shim entry retires and the wrapper moves to the matching MLX-C family — the audit-upstream-surface tool flags both the retireable entry and the still-missing wrapper.

### `MlxEinsumPath`

```rust
pub struct MlxEinsumPath {
    /// Each contraction step's operand positions, in execution order.
    pub steps: Vec<Vec<i32>>,
    /// MLX's human-readable summary of the path.
    pub description: String,
}
```

The contraction order `einsum` would follow for one set of operands.
